threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think getting on the Tube at 5 PM is a good idea. Real locals have a secret bus route or just avoid it altogether.
Last night on the 59, a woman loudly argued with the driver about the 'missing stop'. Turns out she thought it was a Sunday service—classic Brixton confusion.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last week I saw a guy playing the accordion while balancing on a unicycle outside the bakery. That’s when it hit me: I’m home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a café where you can sip coffee while watching street artists paint live murals on the walls next door. Such a vibe!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their unbothered reaction to a dog on the Muni tracks—while newcomers are panicking, we just roll our eyes.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy calmly playing a saxophone on the Muni after a 20-minute delay—the perfect soundtrack to an otherwise chaotic morning.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'tapas' means small plates everywhere. In Gràcia, it’s about community and sharing a table, not just food.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their intense focus on the metro map—like it’s a treasure map rather than just a transit guide.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still hesitate before stepping into the street when the green man flashes—locals just glide across like it’s a free-for-all.
Saw a guy on the 333 serenading a pack of pigeons at Brixton Station like they were his audience. Not even fazed when they ignored him.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a group of kids arguing about whether their Döner was better than the one across the street. That's when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Where else can you find a 24-hour Späti selling odd flavored pickles and homemade currywurst at 3 AM? It’s a slice of life only Berlin gets.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they can name at least three taco trucks but avoid the tourist traps like the plague, especially on a Friday night.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a musician pull out a sax on the bus, started a mini jam session. Some riders groaned, others clapped. Only in the Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to our parks but overlook the small, unique plazas where locals gather. It’s in the quiet corners that you find real community life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You'll see them fumbling with the metro tickets while still holding a map. Locals have long ditched those for their phones.
